Commissioner v. Kowalski, 434 U.S. 77 (1977) — https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/434/77/
[cite: 2]
Internal Revenue Code of 1954, 26 U.S.C. § 61(a) and § 119
original_excerpt:
In Commissioner v. Kowalski, 434 U.S. 77 (1977), the Supreme Court ruled that cash meal allowances paid to state troopers represent realized accessions to wealth over which employees exercise complete dominion, making them includible as gross income under § 61(a).   

The Court explicitly concluded that § 119 applies exclusively to meals furnished in kind on the employer's business premises and does not permit exclusions for cash reimbursements or meal allowances, regardless of whether the payments were provided for the employer's convenience or tied to employment conditions.
fidelity: Regular trooper allowances are income; §119 excludes in-kind meals under its conditions rather than cash reimbursements. Generalization should remain tied to this holding.
scope_note: No ruling that every possible meal-related reimbursement is taxable under every provision; opinion expressly reserves sporadic reimbursement and other grounds for supper-money exclusions.
